abstract: AbstractServing effectively as an expert witness in an IP dispute requires the expert witness to be knowledgable about terminology, legal process, and expectations of their role in prosecuting infringement or disputing the validity of a patent. The author has supported over twenty-five IP litigations since 2008, experience that permits him to offer insights from the perspective of the expert. This talk will discuss, (1) the role of an expert witness in a litigation (in general); (2) terminology specific to an IP matter (including Inter Partes Review, claims construction, person of skill in the art, discovery, prior art, infringement, considerations for obviousness, unenforceability, and trade secret); and finally, (3) the stages of the IP litigation process and expected/typical timelines of each.

topic: 270a- From Lab to Legislation: A ChemE’s Transition from Research to Regulatory Policy and Industry Advocacy

abstract: AbstractThis paper explores the professional journey of a chemical engineer who transitioned from a technical career in research and development and process development/optimization to a chemical industry policy and scientific advocacy. Chemical Engineers, equipped with a strong technical foundation whether at the bachelor's, master's or doctoral levels, can combine their technical expertise and penchant for innovation with a motivation to influence broader industry practices and informed regulatory frameworks. The often interdisciplinary nature of chemical engineering, and unique viewpoint from industry experience, can accelerate and shape sustainable and scientifically informed chemicals management. This paper uses a case example of skills and experience to help other chemical engineers explore transitioning their own career, the impact of engineering expertise in the regulatory arena, and the landscape of chemicals management policy around the world.

abstract: AbstractMy name is Michael Stephenson, and I am an intellectual property attorney at the law firm Buchanan Ingersoll & Rooney PC, in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Before going to law school, I attended the University of Pittsburgh and received a B.S. degree in chemical engineering in 2018. Until my senior year of undergrad, I fully intended on pursuing a traditional career as a practicing engineer. However, while working as a summer intern as a chemical engineering student, I started to have doubts regarding the career path that was best for me. I discussed my dilemma with a professor, and he mentioned that patent law may not only be a potential career path for engineers, but is often times a successful one. I took his advice and jumped straight into law school after receiving my engineering degree, and I graduated from the University of Pittsburgh School of Law in 2021.After getting my law degree, I got a job at Buchanan Ingersoll & Rooney practicing intellectual property law. The vast majority of my practice involves patent prosecution, which generally relates to the process of obtaining patent rights. I get to utilize my chemical engineering knowledge on an everyday basis, as I have regular meetings with inventors to discuss their innovations and how they may be best protected.During my presentation, I’ll give you a more detailed description of how I got where I am now. I’ll then provide more detail on what exactly I do at Buchanan and how I continue to use my chemical engineering degree in a non-traditional manner.

topic: 270c- Breaking Symmetry: Resilient Careers for Unpredictable Futures
date_time:

 -

abstract: AbstractIt’s not what you know, it’s knowing what to do with what you know. In a business landscape where disruptive companies are themselves becoming disrupted or replaced, it’s not sufficient to base career decisions only on title, salary and position. Instead of following the traditional career paths which mirror each other across industries, we explore nonlinear ways of strategizing your career, why applying the knowledge you have is more critical than only focusing on acquiring new knowledge alone. We’ll focus on how to expand your career thinking, growing from short semesters to legacy-building decades and accelerating executive career experiences outside your present professional area to impact future opportunities. Your biggest success may be in a field that doesn’t even exist yet. How will you prepare for industries that have yet to be created?

topic: 508a- Optimal Synthesis and Planning of SustainableChemical Process and Energy Systems
date_time:

 - 
12:15 PM
abstract: AbstractIn this lecture we give an overview on the applications of recent models and algorithms for the discrete and continuous optimization of a variety of challenging applications in the optimal synthesis and planning of sustainable chemical processes and energy systems. We provide an overview of applications of deterministic models based on mixed-integer linear/nonlinear programming (MILP/MINLP), Generalized Disjunctive Programming (GDP) and global optimization techniques, many of which have been developed by chemical engineers in the area of process systems engineering. We first consider applications of MILP in energy systems that include optimization of hydrogen supply chains, and the long term expansion planning of reliable and resilient electric power systems with high penetration of renewables. We also briefly discuss the retrofit of crude oil refineries for processing biomass to produce sustainable aviation fuels. Next, we consider applications of MINLP and GDP that include synthesis of lignocellulosic ethanol, optimization of shale gas infrastructures, and synthesis of intensified distillation columns. We consider next recent algorithms for rigorous global optimization of nonconvex optimization models for which we consider applications in optimal process water networks that involve reuse and recycle, optimal maritime transportation planning under carbon intensity constraints, and optimal design of centralized and distributed manufacturing facilities for biomass production. Finally, we briefly discuss extensions of these models to handle uncertainties. The variety of applications that we cover in this lecture, illustrates the scope that optimization techniques have towards the optimal synthesis and planning of sustainable chemical processes and energy systems.
